<section begin=intro />
Similar to the [[Nervos Mine]], the '''Arc Trap''' is a [[Grineer]] device that attacks hostiles within '''8''' meters via an {{D|Electricity}} arc. The trap can be destroyed by your weapons, generating a burst of electricity that damages and stuns nearby opponents and allies. They will also destroy themselves after 3 seconds of continuous shocking. They were added in {{ver|12.5}} as a replacement to [[Broken Light]]s.<section end=intro />

==Notes==
*Arc Traps can hit cloaked targets, notably {{A|Prowl}}ing {{WF|Ivara}}, even when she is using the {{M|Infiltrate}} augment.
*The blast of the {{Weapon|Penta}} or the {{Weapon|Ogris}} will not destroy the trap, but their projectiles can.
*The traps appear as enemies on the map when using {{M|Enemy Radar}} and similar effects such as Ivara's passive or {{M|Animal Instinct}}.
*Arc traps alert nearby enemies within roughly 25 meters, similar to a [[Noise Level|loud]] weapon fired by a shooting source.
**If the player and all nearby allies are cloaked when the trap goes off, the enemies will be unalerted, even if both they and the Tenno take damage from the arc.
**Destroying the arc trap will not produce the similar noise, instead it only alerts the surrounding enemies that are caught in the electrical blast.
*During [[Invasion]] missions where you're helping the Grineer, Arc Traps will not target the player, but will target any [[Corpus]] unit that comes within range. The player can still destroy them and the final explosion will harm anyone, the player included, as usual.

==Tips==
*They occasionally emit arcing sounds. Use this a cue to locate them, or alternatively use the [[Codex Scanner]] to scan areas you suspect Arc Traps have been placed.
*Since the trap releases an electric burst upon its destruction, it can be used on enemies to stun them.
* When attempting a stealth mission, try to avoid coming into the range of these traps. Once the trap is set off, it will alert any Grineer in the same room.
*They can easily kill players attempting to flee a [[Survival]] mission when the oxygen runs out, as the player will only have 5 points of health after a short period of time after complete oxygen loss.

Nullifier Crewman={{Enemy|name=Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Juno={{Enemy|name=Juno Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Vapos={{Enemy|name=Vapos Nullifier}} |-|Taro={{Enemy|name=Taro Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Axio={{Enemy|name=Axio Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Vorac={{Enemy|name=Vorac Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Orm={{Enemy|name=Orm Nullifier Crewman}} |-|Scrofa={{Enemy|name=Scrofa Obviator}}
{{Codex|Energy shield blocks projectiles and nullifies powers}}
The '''Nullifier Crewman''' is a specialized [[Corpus]] [[Sniper Crewman]] carrying a power disruptor on his back. When alerted, the nullifier deploys an orbiting '''Projector Drone''' that generates a [[Warframes|Warframe]]-suppressing field beneath it. The spherical field not only prevents projectiles from entering (similar to [[Frost]]'s [[Snow Globe]]), but also prevents any Warframe [[abilities]] from being cast within its radius, destroys most powers and cancels out any active buffs as soon as players enter it. Firing at the globe causes it to gradually shrink and eventually dissipate altogether, forcing the drone back into the backpack, from where it will re-emerge after a brief period. The Projector Drone itself resides at all times outside the field, orbiting above the Crewman, therefore destroying it will permanently remove the Crewman's ability to create the barrier.
==Farming Locations== ''These are based on opinions and may not be 100% true. These should be viewed as advice for finding the enemies until better facts are proven.'' ;Normal Nullifier Crewman {{MissionTable|Abaddon|Galatea|Neso}} ==Tactics== *Nullifier bubbles use the following mechanic to determine damage dealt to it: **Nullifier bubbles have a minimum and maximum damage per shot dealt to it – '''100 damage at minimum''', and '''400 damage maximum'''. Any hit that deals less than 100 damage will be buffed to that amount, while any shot that deals more than 400 damage will be nerfed to that amount. The buffed/nerfed damage values are displayed by the damage indicator. ***If the attack deals {{D|Magnetic}} damage, the Nullifier bubble takes '''300 - 1200''' damage instead. **The damage dealt is then altered by the Nullifier bubble's shrink rate per shot, which is '''6%''' of its current size. **The formula for determining damage to the Nullifier bubble is: {{MathText|Damage {{div}} 100 {{mul}} Shrink Rate}}. ***Example A: A {{Weapon|Braton}} hits the bubble for 18 damage. Since the bubble can only receive a minimum of 100 damage, the bubble takes 100 damage from that hit. The damage (100) is then divided by 100, which equals 1.0. This value is then multiplied by the shrink rate of 6% (0.06), giving a value of 0.06, which results in the bubble being reduced by 6% of its current size. ***Example B: An {{Weapon|Opticor}} hits the bubble for 500 damage. Since the bubble can only receive a maximum of 400 damage, the bubble only takes 400 damage from the shot. The calculation is thus: {{MathText|400 {{div}} 100 {{mul}} 0.06 {{eql}} 0.24}}, hence the bubble will shrink by 24% of its current size. **The rate of shrinkage is based off the current size of the bubble. **Hits are calculated per frame (frame rate), and not for each individual pellet within a shot, i.e. a shotgun that shoots 6 pellets dealing 100 damage each for a total of 600 damage is considered as dealing 600 damage, and thus will have its damage nerfed to 400, resulting in a 24% reduction in bubbles. *Due to the Nullifier field having [[Object]] health property which '''nullifies''' [[Critical Hit]] damage, weapons that heavily depend on crits such as {{Weapon|Soma}}, {{Weapon|Synapse}} or {{Weapon|Amprex}} can be less effective against it if the non-critical dps value is too low. **However, the '''Projector Drone''' orbiting above the Crewman '''''is''' vulnerable to Critical damage'', and therefore one is advised to aim for it with weapons relying on crits. *The drone is located near the top of the Nullifier's facing side, and can hide itself on the opposite end of the barrier dome respective to the player if the Nullifier is running/facing away. *Being a sniper unit, Nullifiers are far less accurate up close, but get more accurate at medium and long ranges. *Vapos, Orm, Vorac, Axio and Taro nullifiers will try to get close to enemies and hit them with their 2 [[Prova|Provas]] *Splash damage from explosive weapons and powers originating outside the field are nullified, dealing no damage to anything inside, and each explosion counting as only a single hit to the field. A direct hit from the alternate-fire projectile of a [[Stahlta]] will actually bounce off the field and get deflected elsewhere. *The energy sphere will remove any buffs active on Warframes caught inside it, and will render the Nullifier immune to direct targeting by all Warframe powers, including AoE and indirect powers. The sphere can also deactivate [[Guard Mode]] of a [[Voidrig]]. However, while inside the sphere the Nullifier Crewman will have no protection against weapon attacks, and Warframes can walk through the field at will. *Despite being a [[Sniper Crewman]], the Nullifier Crewmen's behavior is a bit different; they will not attempt to bash enemies who get too close, and much like [[Eximus|Arctic Eximus]] they will not attempt to take cover or run away. Nearby allies will also head inside the Nullifier Crewman's sphere, making it harder to kill them. *Nullifier fields ''absorb'' hitscan projectiles and '''deflect''' physical projectiles. **Certain ability projectiles (e.g. the {{A|Shuriken}} projectiles) can home in on the Nullifier, but if the bubble is present then they will bounce off of it like normal projectiles. *Due to the field having object health, weapons with very large clips, base damage and fast [[fire rate]] are most effective at dealing with Nullifiers. *Using a {{Weapon|Miter}} with the {{M|Neutralizing Justice}} mod can sometimes instantly and permanently destroy the bubble. ==Notes== *While they can be {{A|Mind Control|Mind Controlled}} when their bubbles are down, they will dispel the control when the bubble resumes, regardless of the fact that the Nullifier is now allied and should revert his bubble to dispel enemy powers instead. *Originally, Nullifiers would simply ignore Warframe powers, which was more reasonable in most players' eyes. But they were changed to destroy all abilities on contact, despite some powers becoming physical objects like {{A|Tectonics}} or {{A|Snow Globe}}. *Even augments like {{M|Ice Wave Impedance}} are nullified; the frozen path is destroyed wherever a Nullifier bubble touches. *All of {{WF|Vauban}}'s powers are nullified as well, but only if the Nullifier bubble touches the grenade. *If a Nullifier spawns as an [[Eximus|Arctic Eximus]], It is possible for them to deploy both Snow Globe and their regular Nullifier bubble. *Attacking the bubble will alert the Nullifier. *Bubbles can erode {{WF|Nidus}} mutation stacks when inside. *{{WF|Octavia}}'s {{A|Mallet}} can damage the Nullfier's bubbles, despite being an ability. *Immune to {{D|Lifted}}, {{D|Ragdoll}}, and {{D|Knockdown}} effects while bubble is active. *Currently, Nullifier Crewmen can completely cancel [[Tauron Strike|Tauron Strikes]]. This is likely a bug. ==Tips== *Nullifiers deactivate their bubbles when not alerted. *The Nullifier's bubbles can be destroyed by melee attacks if they connect on the edge of its radius, which can be utilized by abilities such as: **{{WF|Excalibur}}'s {{A|Exalted Blade}} **{{WF|Ivara}}'s {{A|Artemis Bow}} **{{WF|Wukong}}'s {{A|Primal Fury}} **{{WF|Valkyr}}'s {{A|Hysteria}} *{{Weapon|Miter}}'s {{M|Neutralizing Justice}} and {{WF|Hildryn}}'s {{M|Balefire Surge}} augments can instantly destroy nullifier fields. *The minimum amount of regular shots required to break a '''regular Nullfield''' is '''6''' shots and the minimum time to do so is '''~1.5''' seconds. **The maximum damage a shot can deal to a Nullfield is 1200, therefore it must be assumed that a regular Nullfield itself has at most {{MathText|6 {{mul}} 1200 {{eql}} 7200 health}}. Hence dealing more than {{MathText|7200 {{div}} 1.5 {{eql}} 4800 damage per second}} will not benefit dealt DPS further. A Nullfield receives a minimum of 300 and a maximum of 1200 damage per shot. To burst it apart with a maximum effective DPS within the minimum time lapse given, a fire rate of at least {{MathText|4800 {{div}} 1200 {{eql}} 4 shots per second}} is required if the damage per shot exceeds 1200. Shots below 300 damage requires at least {{MathText|4800 {{div}} 300 {{eql}} 16 shots per second}}. Multishots shall be counted in if given. **If the damage per shot is in between those thresholds, the necessary fire rate against a regular Nullfield can be broadly calculated by this formula: {{MathText|4800 {{div}} Damage per shot {{eql}} Minimum fire rate}}. **Take care of '''not''' using critical hit multipliers in the above formula. **Note that certain beam-weapons like {{Weapon|Ignis}}, {{Weapon|Amprex}} or {{Weapon|Quanta Vandal}} have different properties when it comes to fire rate and damage per shot. The former for example has a ramped damage output (in the manner of Aksomati's ramping ammo spool). ==Trivia== *Nullifier Crewmen seem to wear the same uniform that [[The Sergeant]] wears, albeit with yellow chest straps rather than white ones. *Oddly, the Codex image of Nullifier Crewmen seems to represent a standard Crewman with a black uniform and a jetpack used by the three [[Ranger]] variants in [[Archwing]] missions, whilst the in-game model has an additional helmet extension and a unique "core" pack on its back. *When summoned from {{WF|Nekros}}, their bubbles will be the caster's energy color. *A variant of the Nullifier Crewman can appear as a [[Capture]] target, the [[Nullifier Target]]. *Despite using a [[Lanka]] which is {{D|Electricity}} based, it deals mostly {{D|Puncture}} damage as shown by {{M|Adaptation}}. *In the [[Deepmines]], Nullifier Crewmen are titled as Obviators, but otherwise function identically. ==Media== Nullifier_Crewman.jpg|Nullifier Crewman shown in the codex DescriptionLiesNormal.jpeg|Showing that Nullifier crewmen can be controlled, despite their description ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|44}} *Fixed swapping between Sons while entering a Nullifier bubble causing the Inactive Son’s abilities to be permanently disabled. {{ver|43.5}} *Fixed swapping between Sons while entering a Nullifier Bubble resulting in the Secondary Son permanently losing access to his Abilities. {{ver|41.0.3}} *Fixed Nullifier bubbles having collision for player cameras. {{ver|40.0.3}} *Fixed overlapping Nullifier bubbles in Limbo's Cataclysm causing Nullifiers to become invulnerable to attacks. {{ver|40.0.2}} *Fixed Ivara's Concentrated Arrow crashing the game if shot at a Nullifier Bubble. {{ver|40}} ;NULLIFIER BUBBLE INTERACTION CHANGES Changed how the following Warframe’s Abilities interact with Nullifier bubbles. '''Frost’s Snow Globe:''' Nullifier bubbles now drain Snow Globe's life by 20% per second, and cannot gain strength when a Nullifier bubble is touching it. '''Limbo’s Cataclysm:''' Now shrinks 4 times faster when touching a Nullifier orb, instead of being removed instantly. '''Mag’s Magnetize:''' Magnetize’s Duration expires 4x faster, but ends instantly if the Nullifier bubble touches the center. '''Oberon’s Hallowed Ground:''' No longer removes Hallowed Ground, but protects enemies from Hallowed Ground’s effects. '''Oraxia’s Webbed Embrace:''' No longer removes Webbed Embrace, but protects enemies from Webbed Embrace’s effects. {{ver|37}} *Fixed the Larkspur Archgun randomly being unable to damage Nullifier Bubbles. {{ver|36}}
'''Magnetic Changes:''' *Damage to Nullifier Bubbles has been increased **Minimum Damage raised to 300 Damage per shot. **Maximum Damage raised to 1200 Damage per shot. ***Additionally, we now show the minimum and maximum damage numbers against Nullifier Bubbles, with Magnetic attacks displaying the buffed damage shown above, while non-Magnetic sources will display the original, unbuffed damage. ****Known issue: Clients see the incorrectly unbuffed damage from Magnetic sources, which is strictly a UI/visual bug. Magnetic sources will continue to deal increased damage towards Nullifier Bubbles despite the incorrect numbers displayed. We will look to resolve this in a future Hotfix/Update. {{ver|31.6.1}} *Fixed script error that could occur when an enemy’s Nullifier dome is destroyed. {{ver|31.5.4}} *Fixed script error related to nullifier bubbles. {{ver|29.10}} *Fixed the Larkspur beam (when used as a Heavy Weapon) occasionally not dealing damage to Nullifier bubbles. {{ver|19.5.7}} *Fixed Warframe abilities appearing blocked (but still castable) after simultaneously being nullified and falling off the edge. {{ver|19.4.2}} *Changed Nullifier Bubbles to be deactivated when they aren’t alert. Hurray stealth! *Improved the ability for arrows from Bow weapons to hit and deal damage to Nullifier Bubbles. *Removed the ability for Nullifier Bubbles to be dispelled by Radial Damage. {{ver|Specters of the Rail}} ;Abilities & Augments vs Nullifiers *Abilities will not affect players or enemies within a Nullifier bubble. *Effects of an ability on both players and enemies will be removed when entering Nullifier bubbles. *A Warframe’s active abilities will be deactivated upon entering a Nullifier bubble. *Projectiles spawned by an ability will be deflected when they encounter a Nullifier bubble. For example, Ember’s Fireball and Ash’s Shuriken will be deflected. *Abilities that exist independent of their creator will not be deactivated if the Warframe enters a nullifier, but will be destroyed if touched by the bubble itself. For example, Frost’s Snowglobe will not disappear when Frost enters the bubble, but will be destroyed if the bubble comes into contact with the Snowglobe sphere. ;Other Changes *Polished the hit detection of melee weapons within Nullifier bubbles. Some weapons, like the Tonbo for example, would strike the Nullifier bubble first, followed by the Nullifier agent in the same strike. However, the damage would only result on the bubble! The weapons can now strike both the bubble and the agent on the same strike, and the agent will take damage as long you are inside the bubble for the attack. {{ver|15.10.2}} *Increased Affinity received for killing Nullifier Crewman to 150, and increased Affinity gained for killing Corrupted Nullifiers to 500. }} ==See also== *[[Corrupted Nullifier]], a Corrupted version found in the [[Void]]. {{CorpusNav}} [[es:Tripulante Anulador]] [[fr:Homme d'Équipage Zéro]] [[Category:Corpus]] [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Update 15]] [[ru:Нуллификатор Корпуса]] [[uk:Рядовий-нуліфікатор]]

{{Codex|Infect your foes with this spore-scattering pistol. Headshots burrow in and explode, releasing spore clouds that seek out nearby enemies.}}
'''Zymos''' is an [[Infested]] pistol that releases explosive spores. On [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]], the spores burrow into the target, stunning and dealing continuous damage before exploding to release 6 additional spores that [[homing|seek]] nearby enemies.

==Characteristics==
This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.

'''Advantages:'''
*High {{D|Puncture}} and good {{D|Impact}} damage – effective against [[armor]] and [[shield]]s.
*Above average [[critical multiplier]].
*Very high [[status chance]].
*Shots have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc.
*Shots explode in a '''3.3''' meter radius upon impact with a surface or enemy, inflicting {{D|Toxin}} damage.
**Innate {{D|Toxin}} damage – bypasses [[Shield]]s.
**[[Enemy Body Parts|Headshots]] stun targets for '''1.1''' second and deals continuous damage before exploding for '''953''' {{D|Toxin}} damage and knocking down the initial target, then scattering '''6''' spores that home-in on nearby enemies within 20 meters, dealing '''23''' damage on contact with a guaranteed chance to proc {{D|Impact}} on targets over 7m away from the initial target in addition to '''333''' {{D|Toxin}} damage in a radius each.
**Initial hit and explosion apply status separately.
**Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
**Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}).
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} and {{Pol|Naramon}} polarities.

'''Disadvantages:'''
*Very low [[critical chance]].
*Very low [[fire rate]].
*Very slow [[reload speed]].
*All projectiles have travel time.
*Explosions inflict [[Stagger|self-stagger]].
*Explosion has linear damage falloff from 100% to 70% from central impact.
*[[Enemy Body Parts|Headshot]] explosion delay allows enemies to move out of the explosion range.
*Extremely low ammo capacity; requires just 3 reloads to fully deplete all ammo reserves.

==Acquisition==
Zymos is acquired by reaching '''Rank 1 - Stranger''' with the [[Entrati]]. [[Father]] sells the main blueprint for {{sc|2,000}} and component blueprints for {{sc|1,000}}; a total of {{sc|4,000}} is needed for all parts. The main blueprint is also offered as a rank-up reward.

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
{{UpdateMe}}
*One barrel blueprint is required to reach '''Rank 1 - Clearance: Agnesis''' with the [[Necraloid]].
*[[Punch Through]] has '''no''' effect on projectiles.
*Since headshots stun the enemy to then release the spore projectiles, if an enemy cannot be 'stunned' ([[Demolisher]], enemies with [[Overguard]]) then the spores will never spawn.
*Initial '''953''' {{D|Toxin}} damage explosion will almost always be affected by headshot and headcrit bonuses, receiving double damage in addition to double critical multiplier.
*{{text||Second-stage projectiles|hover=The Scattering Spores}} from the initial explosion are affected differently by mods and buffing effects.
**Base damage from mods like {{M|Hornet Strike}} and {{M|Magnum Force}} apply to the {{text||23 contact damage|hover=50% Slash, 50% Puncture}}, but '''do not''' apply to the '''333''' {{D|Toxin}} explosion.
***Spores randomly select enemies within 20m of the host enemy. This range is '''not''' affected by {{M|Fulmination}}.
***Spore contact damage has a guaranteed chance to proc {{D|Impact}} on enemies more than '''7m''' away from the host enemy, but has '''0% '''natural status chance to proc modded elements.
**[[Elemental mods]] apply normally.
**[[Faction Damage]] applies normally.
**[[Multishot]] increases the number of initial projectiles of each spore, but not the 6 spores that are released from each explosion.
**[[Critical Damage]] mods and absolute critical chance bonuses are applied twice.
<!--
**Critical Chance and Critical Damage bonuses are applied '''<u>squared</u>'''.
**{{text||Flat Critical Chance Bonuses|hover=Harrow's Covenant, Adarza's Cat's Eye, Arcane Avenger}} are '''<u>applied twice</u>'''. They are multiplied by modded critical chance once, and then added after that.
***{{MathText|Critical Chance {{Eql}} ((5% {{Mul}} (1 + Modded Crit Chance)) + Flat Crit Chance) {{Mul}} (1 + Modded Crit Chance) + Flat Crit Chance}}
***{{MathText|Critical Damage {{Eql}} 2.3 {{Mul}} (1 + Modded Crit Damage){{exp|2}}}}
**For example, with {{M|Cat's Eye}}, {{M|Pistol Gambit}} and {{M|Target Cracker}}, the secondary projectiles have: 
***Critical Chance: {{Math| (({{text||5%|hover=Zymos's base critical chance}} {{Mul}} (1 + {{M|Pistol Gambit|120%}})) + {{M|Cat's Eye|60%}}) {{Mul}} (1 + {{M|Pistol Gambit|120%}}) + {{M|Cat's Eye|60%}}|mt=y|p=y}}
-->
***Critical Multiplier: {{Math| {{text||2.3|hover=Zymos's base critical multiplier}} {{Mul}} (1 + {{M|Target Cracker|60%}}){{exp|2}}|mt=y|m=y|round=0.01}}
**Shooting the initial projectile through [[Buffing Fields]] will '''not''' affect the secondary projectiles.
***If a [[Buffing Field]] is positioned so that the secondary projectiles pass through it, they will gain the bonuses.
**Spores will still be generated even if the host enemy dies from the initial headshot.

==Tips==
*{{M|Trick Mag}} in the Exilus slot or [[Cyte-09]]'s [[Resupply]] will make up for the low maximum ammo.
*The low fire rate, lack of {{D|Slash}} damage, and forced {{D|Impact}} procs on both the main projectile and homing spores make {{M|Hemorrhage}} a viable option, especially if the Zymos has been modded to deal {{D|Viral}} damage.
*Due to the unusual nature of the weapon's critical scaling, critical modifiers are very effective despite the 5% base crit chance.
**Flat Critical Chance bonuses from {{WF|Harrow}}'s {{A|Covenant}}, {{Companion|Adarza Kavat}}'s {{M|Cat's Eye}}, {{Arcane|Secondary Enervate}}, and {{Arcane|Arcane Avenger}} are affected once by multiplicative Critical Chance bonuses before being applied again.
*{{WF|Nidus}} and {{WF|Xaku}} can use {{A|Parasitic Link}} and {{A|The Lost|Gaze}} respectively to turn a single enemy into an invulnerable spore "fountain" as both abilities keep their victims upright and invincible for their durations. Xaku in particular can prolong Gaze's duration via {{A|The Vast Untime}} on top of Gaze reducing the defenses of any enemy in its range.
**{{A|Well of Life}} is a subsumable option that can also immobilize an enemy for headshots.

==Bugs==
*In multiplayer, poor to moderate network conditions can cause spores to never appear, despite landing headshots. Spore explosions also never occur regardless of network conditions.

==Trivia==
*The Zymos was first seen and wielded by the [[Zealot Proselytizer]] in the third episode of ''[[Nightwave/Series_2|Nightwave: Series 2 – The Emissary]]''.
*Upon performing a headshot on an enemy, the enemy's head with swell up with an audible inflating noise before the spores explode. The inflation is subtle compared to the more drastic effects of the {{Weapon|Nukor}}, and quickly reset upon the explosion.
*Zym/o is a word part meaning Enzyme or Ferment.

{{Infobox | Box title=Overguard | image=Eximus Overguard.png | caption=An Eximus unit with Overguard health |header text=Information |Row 1 title=Icon |Row 1 info=[[File:Overguard.png|class=icon light-invert]] [[File:OverguardOutlineDark_d.png|class=icon]] |Row 2 title=Introduced |Row 2 info={{Ver|31.5}} }} {{Quote|Overguard grants additional Health protection and Knockdown immunity as long as an amount remains.|In-Game Description}} '''Overguard''' is a special [[Hit Points|health buffer]] that grants immunity to most crowd control effects. __TOC__ {{clr}} ==Mechanics== {{HealthModifierTable|Overguard}} Overguard is an additional layer of defense that protects [[Health]] and/or [[Shield]]s from being damaged. It is neutral to all damage types except for a '''50%''' vulnerability from {{D|Void}} damage, though there are a few sources that increase damage dealt to Overguard: *{{D|Magnetic}} [[Status Effect]] amplifies all damage dealt to Overguard in the same way it does to Shields: '''100%''' damage on the first stack, '''25%''' on subsequent stacks up to a maximum of '''325%''' after 10 stacks. In addition, when Overguard breaks, the target receives {{D|Electricity}} damage equal to '''3%''' of their total Overguard per {{D|Magnetic}} stack up to a maximum of '''30%''' at 10 stacks. *[[Damage Vulnerability]] applies normally to Overguard. *Beast [[Companion]] ([[Kubrow]]s, [[Kavat]]s, [[Predasite]]s, and [[Vulpaphyla]]s)'s {{M|Assassin Posture}} increases their damage to Overguard by '''300%'''. *{{Companion|Sunika Kubrow}}'s {{M|Unleashed}} increases their damage to Overguard by '''300%'''. *{{WF|Oberon}}'s {{A|Smite}} instantly removes Overguard. *{{WF|Vauban}}'s {{A|Photon Strike}} deals '''200%''' more damage to Overguard. *[[Hound (Companion)|Hound]]'s {{M|Null Audit}} removes '''50%''' of an [[Eximus]]'s Overguard. *{{Arcane|Secondary Fortifier}} lets secondary weapons and [[Arch-gun]]s deal up to '''8x''' increased damage to enemy Overguard. Overguard is '''not''' affected by [[Damage Reduction]] from armor or abilities such as {{A|Splinter Storm}} or [[Damage Type Modifier|Damage type resistance]] effects such as {{M|Adaptation}} and {{WF|Caliban}}'s [[Caliban/Abilities#Passive|passive]]. However, abilities or effects with [[Damage Redirection]], such as {{A|Link}}, {{A|Warding Halo}}, or {{M|Shield of Shadows}} will apply their effect to Overguard. [[Maneuvers#Rolling|Rolling]] will also apply its damage reduction to Overguard. Enemies can still have their shields and [[armor]] stripped while their Overguard is active. ===Player=== On players, Overguard will negate all [[Status Effect]]s, including {{D|Stagger}} and {{D|Knockdown}}. It additionally has a '''0.5''' second invulnerability gate when fully depleted, preventing any excess damage from leaking into their shield or health pool. Even enemy crowd control effects that still affect players with {{M|Primed Sure Footed}} (such as fire waves by Arson Eximus) will be ignored with Overguard. However, grapple hooks from enemies such as a {{E|Scorpion}} will still interrupt the player for a moment and pull them in. Only Warframes, [[Companion]]s, [[Specter]]s, and [[Eidolon Lure]]s are able to receive Overguard. Consequently, it '''cannot''' be given to [[Defense Objects]]. If the user has no [[Shield]]s active ({{WF|Inaros}} and {{WF|Nidus}} by default), [[Energy]] conversion from damage to [[Health]] effects ({{M|Rage}}, {{M|Hunter Adrenaline}}, {{M|Necramech Rage}}, and {{M|Kinetic Diversion}}) will allow damage to Overguard granted from an ally to be converted to energy. {{WF|Kullervo}}, despite having no shields, cannot reliably benefit from this due to receiving Overguard for himself from {{A|Recompense}}. ===Enemy=== On enemies, they can receive [[Status Effect]]s but while their Overguard is active they will completely ignore the crowd control effects of {{D|Stagger}}, {{D|Knockdown}}, {{D|Stun}}, {{A|Mind Control}}, {{D|Confusion}} (including {{D|Radiation}} procs), {{D|Slow}}, {{D|Ragdoll}}, {{D|Blind}}, and {{D|Lifted}}, and can normally only receive a maximum of 4 {{D|Cold}} procs.
Enemies do not have any invulnerability gating when their Overguard is depleted. Overguard is independent of [[Enemy Level Scaling|enemy health and shield scaling]]. Overguard will scale by level but will be the same amount across all Eximus enemy types. Because of their immunity to crowd control, Overguarded enemies are a threat that should be prioritized; crowd control will still affect their allies and they will still target {{D|Confusion|Confused}} units which helps level the playing field. If afflicted by {{D|Radiation}}, their allies without Overguard can target them which in turn causes the Overguarded enemy to fire back. In the case of {{E|Ancient Protector}} and {{E|The Severed Warden}}, which provide Overguard to their own allies but not themselves while alive, they will still receive crowd control as normal and should be targeted instead. Shooting off a {{E|Nox}}'s helmet will immediately remove their Overguard. ====Scaling==== {{Transclude|Enemy Level Scaling#Overguard}} ==Enemies with Overguard== *All [[Eximus]] except [[Archwing]], [[Warden]], and [[Guardsman#Prosecutor Variant|Prosecutor]] Eximus units. The conversations regarding Dante’s abilities with Overguard became a driving factor to look at these interactions and find ways in which we can make them work to benefit co-op play. '''Chroma’s Vex Armor''' Previously, Overguard would prevent Chroma from benefiting from his Vex Armor buffs (since it blocked damage on Health and Shields). So, in an effort to create a more co-op friendly experience between the two, we’ve made the following change: '''Now, Rage and Hunter Adrenaline can convert the Damage on Overguard granted by allies to Energy while Shields are inactive.''' This allows shield-less Warframes, such as '''Inaros''' and '''Nidus''', to be able to regenerate Energy via these Mods when they would have previously been blocked by Overguard granted by allies. Now that players have access to Overguard consistently, we have made some adjustments to improve the quality of life in this new health state: Consistent Proc Immunity
Due to the variety of sources of Overguard, there were occasionally inconsistencies in how it behaved in regard to Proc Immunity. With Echoes of Duviri, all sources of Player Overguard will offer Full Proc Immunity while active. Overguard Depletion Protection
Similar to Shields, Player Overguard will now offer a brief moment of invulnerability (currently 0.5s) once depleted. This window will prevent players with Overguard from being one-shot, as damage to Overguard will no longer carry over into your Health or Shield pool once depleted. Upon launch, we will closely monitor feedback on this mechanic change to see if further adjustments are needed. NOTE: This Overguard Depletion Protection applies only to Player Overguard, not Overguard seen on enemies. Hit Impact Visuals
Similar to taking damage to your Health or your Shields, Overguard now has its own unique appearance when attacked. Damage will no longer cause blood splatters while Overguard is active, and we have added a unique metallic hit effect that better communicates having a layered shell protecting you. Additionally, players will no longer flinch while taking damage with Overguard active.
